source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Change all/random setting to non-default in this BIOS function.
3. Save and reboot.
4. Boot in to BIOS and  check your setting still exist.
5. Press load default,save and reboot.
6. Boot in to BIOS,setting in this function should match the SPEC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error log happen.
2. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
3. Check your setting still exist.
4. The default setting should matches SPEC."

original_test_intent: Verify that approved UEFI Variables Protection settings persist across save/reboot and return to SPEC defaults after Load Default without corrupting NVRAM variables, boot entries, Secure Boot state or recovery capability.
original_method: Change fields on the UEFI Variables Protection page, save/reboot and verify persistence; then Load Default, save/reboot and compare with SPEC while checking logs, boot and management health.
manual_activity: A human must operate the protection page, execute both save/reboot phases, select Load Default and inspect firmware values. Automated variable inventory can only support those observations.
required_inputs: Named protection fields with baseline, safe non-default and SPEC-default values
Affected variable namespaces, boot entries and Secure Boot/key scope
Read-only NVRAM/boot/security baseline and approved backup handling
Console/operator, stable power and OOB/vendor recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or attempt unspecified variable/key protection changes.
Do not write, delete or enroll UEFI variables, boot entries or keys as an implicit verification step.
Preserve recovery media/path and confirm protected settings will not block required restoration writes.
Stop on boot-entry/key delta, rejected required recovery write, boot or management loss.
Restore the approved final protection state.
agent_execution_scope: Collect approved read-only UEFI variable metadata, boot-entry, Secure Boot, OS boot-mode and BMC health evidence.
Compare firmware captures and inventories against the field/effect matrix.
Do not modify variables/keys/boot entries, drive BIOS or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Define/approve the protection field/default/effect matrix and recovery-write plan.
Perform/capture the non-default persistence and default-restoration phases.
Evaluate firmware, boot and security evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects agent execution of the firmware UI. No source command exists; any UEFI inventory command must be read-only, approved for the OS and must not be turned into a write probe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the manual protection-page workflow and use read-only variable/boot/Secure Boot inventory as supporting evidence; never substitute OS variable writes or key enrollment.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source two-phase sequence, no-script state and 5/20-minute fields are preserved; all/random is retained as source but bounded out of execution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each approved protection value to affected variable namespaces and permitted/denied operations; capture firmware values plus read-only boot/Secure Boot inventory at baseline, non-default persistence, default restoration and final state without injecting writes.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact UEFI implementation and installed boot/security stack.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/firmware, BMC, OS and inventory-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform UEFI Variables Protection specification and approved boot/Secure Boot recovery procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds variable/key scope and non-destructive evidence boundaries while preserving the two firmware transitions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; it avoids unapproved destructive probes and requires project-approved behavior tests separately if writes are essential.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Protection semantics, variable/key scope, defaults and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Read-only inventory cannot by itself prove every protection enforcement path; any write-negative test needs its own named disposable target and approval.

project_override_considerations: The project defines the safe fields and whether a separate disposable-variable enforcement check is authorized. If not, completion covers persistence/default restoration only and must not claim comprehensive protection enforcement.
expected_evidence: Firmware identity, approval, baseline and recovery readiness
First save/reboot persistence and read-only UEFI/boot/security inventory
Load Default, second save/reboot, SPEC comparison and boot/management health
Final protection/boot state, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently describe persistence and SPEC-default restoration. Missing protection semantics and variable scope are readiness inputs rather than conflicting source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The firmware transition intent is clear. Exact fields, defaults and recovery scope gate execution but do not permanently block the library definition.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees with manual classification and adds the missing NVRAM/boot/key safety boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its variable inventory, recovery-write and final-state controls while applying V3.1 readiness semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates safe persistence/default coverage from any additional destructive enforcement probe.

review_improvement: Prevents a protection-setting review from silently writing critical NVRAM or Secure Boot objects and makes recovery-write availability an explicit safety dependency.
independent_technical_reasoning: The decisive settings and observations are in firmware and require human navigation, so MANUAL ONLY is correct. Read-only OS evidence can expose collateral changes but cannot replace the page behavior.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat protection changes, reboot or default load after any variable/key/boot anomaly; preserve inventories and firmware captures and obtain engineer disposition.
